newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable after Thai shock.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable after Thai shock.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Wednesday after the market recovered from an early shock generated by turmoil in the baht.
Thailand set a fresh foreign exchange policy on Wednesday by letting its currency float against the dollar, prompting a slew of baht selling and sending jitters through the region.
However, the rupiah emerged unscathed from the turbulence, staging a strong comeback with an upward trend.
Dealers said the market shrugged off a possible spillover effect as economists hailed strong fundamentals shown by the country's latest macroeconomic indicators.

Spot rupiah, due next Monday following a public holiday in the United States on Friday, was quoted at 2,433.0/33.25 against the dollar at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,432.5/33.5. The rupiah tumbled to a low of 2,445 on selling by offshore players on rumours of a baht devaluation. It recovered after Thailand announced its managed float policy.

Analysts said the Indonesian economy was stronger than that of Thailand, with the country enjoying a healthy trade surplus, sufficient foreign exchange reserves, a manageable current account deficit, low inflation and an eight-percent central bank intervention band.
They said those indicators helped the central bank to comfortably absorb external shocks and internal uncertainty induced during the May general elections.
"I am quite surprised how well the rupiah held up," said Daragh Maher, an economist at ING Barings, adding that previous pressures on the rupiah were election-related.

"Over the last two to three months when other currencies in the region were under a lot of pressure by virtue of the baht, actually the pressure we have seen on the rupiah had been more election-related," Maher said.
He said with the election out of the way people were more comfortable with rupiah risk and that helped explain the relatively strong rupiah performance.
Economists said the rupiah might gradually drift towards the strong end of the central bank's intervention band when the Thai baht settles.

One U.S. bank dealer said there was also speculation in the market of a possible dollar-rupiah band widening ahead of the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI) donor meeting in Tokyo later this month.
The World Bank, which coordinates the CGI, said in a report on Indonesia last month that some countries had a wider intervention band but did not specifically suggest that Jakarta follow suit.
But central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said it was not good sense to follow what other people were doing.
"This kind of argument is weak. That is not good economic policy that just because other poeple have 15 percent we have to go to 15 percent," Djiwandono said.
Dealers said the rupiah remained firm, also shrugging off excess rupiah supply in the money market. Overnight rates fell to four percent from 11.0/12.0 percent in the morning.
Dealers said overnight dollars had also stabilised to six percent. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,432.00/32.35 and 2,433.5/34.00, respectively.
One-month swaps were at 12.0/13.0, two at 26.5/27.5, three at 38.0/39.0 and six at 79.0/81.0 points.
The central bank set its intervention band at 2,427/2,619 and the conversion band at 2,427/2,475 on Wednesday.
